title: Variables
description: One NAME=value per line. They come after the project's shared variables, and reach the container at its next deploy.
descriptionBuilt: One NAME=value per line. They come after the project's shared variables, and reach the container at its next deploy. They do not reach a build.
savedHint: They take effect at the next deploy.
invalidLine: Line {{line}} needs to look like NAME=value.

file.label: Also write the build variables to a file
file.pathInvalid: Use a path inside the source, such as .env.
file.inImage: Put this file in the build context
file.inImageOff: It stays out of the context, so no COPY can put it in the image. A Dockerfile reads it with RUN --mount=type=secret,id=env-file,dst=.env. Other builders do not get it.
file.inImageOn: A COPY of the context puts it in an image layer, where anyone with the image can read it. It holds only build variables.

interpolation.label: Fill in $(PROJECT_NAME), $(SERVICE_NAME) and $(PRIMARY_DOMAIN)
interpolation.hint: Off, those stay exactly as you type them. Every other $(...) and ${...} is always left alone.

revealHint: Showing these values is recorded in the activity log.

build.title: Build
build.description: What a build gets. Nothing in the container's variables reaches it on its own.

inherited.title: Still sharing its variables with the build
inherited.body: This service was building before build variables existed, so its builds still get its runtime variables, sealed ones aside. A value a Dockerfile declares as ARG stays in the image's history. Set what the build needs below, then stop sharing them.
inherited.stopped: Runtime variables no longer reach the build
inherited.confirmTitle: Stop sharing runtime variables with the build?
inherited.confirmBody: After this the build only gets what is set for it here. A build that relied on anything else may start failing, or start working differently.

variables.title: Build variables
variables.hint: One NAME=value per line. They reach the build as arguments, and what a Dockerfile declares as ARG can be read back from the image's history, so nothing secret goes here.

secrets.title: Build secrets
secrets.hint: For a build step that needs a credential. A Dockerfile reads one with RUN --mount=type=secret,id=NAME. It is never part of the image and can't be read back. Nixpacks can't take one without writing it into the image, so it gets none.
secrets.name: Name
secrets.nameInvalid: Use letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
secrets.removeHint: Builds will no longer get this secret. Its value can't be recovered.
secrets.nameHint: The name a build step reads it by.
secrets.valueHint: Kept sealed and given to the build only.
